title: The training principles series: bodybuilder proportions
summary: NH argues bodybuilder proportions are defined by big limbs (arms and legs), a small waist and defined core, deliberately abnormal. Natural bodybuilding has been co-opted by powerlifting/strongman YouTube, producing big-trunk physiques with afterthought arms ('spider body'). Natural lifters build legs well through compounds but neglect calves, which should be trained from intermediate onward.

claims.claim: Being big and muscular doesn't make you a bodybuilder; a bodybuilder physique has a specific look.
Whatever your frame and limb length, you can look like a bodybuilder depending on how you train.
For hypertrophy, tonnage matters more than strength.
The limbs make the bodybuilder physique: there is no bodybuilder with small arms, even if some have dominant triceps or lagging forearms.
Legs mattered less in old-school bodybuilding; there is no such thing as legs too big as long as it's muscle, not fat.
Someone with a big back and chest but no arms looks big but not like a bodybuilder.

Natural bodybuilding is barely represented on YouTube; powerlifting and strongman channels have taken over hypertrophy and physique advice, so YouTube fitness physiques have big trunks and legs but afterthought arms.
Everything from shoulder to hand must be developed; he prefers dominant triceps long head and biceps, but still trains delts and forearms.
If you want an aesthetic physique, put more effort and thought into training the arms.
Natural powerlifting has mastered building big legs, because legs respond extremely well to compounds; quads can be developed solely through them.
Many naturals, including him, lack calves, and big upper legs make calves look smaller; he's catching up after years of not training them.
Start training calves early: optional as a novice making strength gains, but immediately once intermediate, or you'll regret it.
Not training your limbs is a sin: too big a trunk makes limbs look smaller, producing the 'spider body' (massive chest, spaghetti arms).
Bodybuilder proportions: big limbs, as small a waist as your structure allows, a defined core, looking out of proportion.
Being a bodybuilder means being abnormal; if it looked like everyone else it would just be normal.
Big arms are what normal people lack: many look big from storing fat in the trunk or legs, but few have arm size, so a natural with big arms is already above the curve.
